papers.title: Super-resolved digital terrain models for GEDI geolocation correction: agreement with airborne LiDAR DTM-based corrections at the beam level, not the footprint level
papers.summary: The Global Ecosystem Dynamics Investigation (GEDI) mission measures three-dimensional forest structure with a LiDAR aboard the International Space Station. GEDI observations have geolocation errors of about 10 m, which cause misalignment with other remote sensing data and reduce the accuracy of downstream tasks. Matching GEDI ground elevations against high-resolution digital terrain models (DTMs) from airborne LiDAR is one way to correct these errors, but such DTMs exist in few regions. To widen this method's applicability, we super-resolved a more widely available low-resolution DTM and used it for the matching. Our question is whether a super-resolved DTM yields the same correction as a 1 m-resolution airborne LiDAR DTM and, if not, why. In steep forests of western Japan, we super-resolved an existing 10 m-resolution DTM to 1 m. Improving its accuracy required fusion with a global 30 m-resolution DTM from a different source. Using the resulting DTM, we corrected GEDI observation positions first by a single shift per ground track, then per observation. For most tracks, the shifts nearly matched those from the airborne LiDAR DTM, likely because DTM errors canceled out across many observations. Per-observation corrections, however, did not match. At a single observation, the error does not cancel out and is too large for the correction. This error likely originates mainly from the input DTM. Therefore, even without a 1 m-resolution DTM, a roughly 10 m-resolution DTM, fused with a global DTM and super-resolved to 1 m, should yield track-wise corrections nearly matching those from a 1 m-resolution DTM.

papers.title: AdaptivePnP: Fast Auto-Tuned Plug-and-Play for Deconvolution
papers.summary: Plug-and-play (PnP) methods reconstruct images by alternating a data-fitting step with an image denoiser. Their performance depends on two parameters: the step size $γ$ and the measurement noise level $σ$. In practice, $γ$ is often tuned by grid search over validation images and must be retuned whenever the problem setting changes, and $σ$ is assumed known or estimated separately. We propose AdaptivePnP, a PnP framework that jointly estimates $σ$ and $γ$ at every iteration from the data-fitting residual. To do so, we apply the PnP virtual model to the data-fitting proximal map and show that the residual is zero-mean Gaussian with covariance parameterized by $γ$ and $σ$. However, when one parameter is much larger than the other, the residual carries little information about the smaller one and using the maximum likelihood (ML) estimator can degrade the PnP iterations. We therefore introduce the identifiable maximum likelihood (IML) estimator, which restricts the ML estimator to an identifiable window in which the normalized Cramér--Rao bound of every parameter is bounded by a user-specified tolerance. For the virtual model, this window is an interval of ratios $ρ= γ/σ$, so computing the IML estimate reduces to a one-dimensional search over $ρ$. We apply AdaptivePnP to two standard PnP methods, yielding algorithms that require neither a tuned $γ$ nor a known $σ$. On image deblurring and super-resolution, AdaptivePnP matches or outperforms PnP baselines tuned with the true $σ$. Code is available at https://github.com/hdubasullivan/AdaptivePnP.

papers.title: Tomographic Sparse View Selection using the View Covariance Loss
papers.summary: Standard computed tomography (CT) reconstruction algorithms such as filtered back projection (FBP) and Feldkamp-Davis-Kress (FDK) require many views for producing high-quality reconstructions, which can slow image acquisition and increase cost in non-destructive evaluation (NDE) applications. Over the past 20 years, a variety of methods have been developed for computing high-quality CT reconstructions from sparse views. However, the problem of how to select the best views for CT reconstruction remains open. In this paper, we present a novel view covariance loss (VCL) function that measures the joint information of a set of views by approximating the normalized mean squared error (NMSE) of the reconstruction. We present fast algorithms for computing the VCL along with an algorithm for selecting a subset of views that approximately minimizes its value. Our experiments on simulated and measured data indicate that for a fixed number of views our proposed view covariance loss selection (VCLS) algorithm results in reconstructions with lower NRMSE, fewer artifacts, and greater accuracy than current alternative approaches.

papers.title: Beyond Segmentation: Enriching ImageCAS with Coronary Ostia Landmarks, Rooted Centerline Graphs, and Open-Weight Localization Models
papers.summary: Coronary ostia and centerlines are key reference points for automated analysis of coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA), from surgical planning to intraoperative vessel tracking. However, the only public ostium annotations cover 77 non-gated aortic scans, not CCTA, while CAT08 and ASOCA (32 and 40 CCTA scans) mark the ostia only implicitly, as centerline start points. This work enriches ImageCAS, the largest public dataset for coronary artery segmentation, with ostium annotations for its 1000 patients and centerline graphs rooted at these new ostia, making it, to the authors' knowledge, the largest public dataset for ostium localization and the only one with centerlines following the official ImageCAS masks and starting at annotated ostia. Three annotators marked each ostium in the first 500 volumes; in the next 500, the candidates of a model trained on the first batch were corrected (human-in-the-loop). Six 3D localization models, trained on ImageCAS, CAT08 and ASOCA, were benchmarked on 58 held-out volumes (50 ImageCAS, 4 CAT08, 4 ASOCA). SwinUNETR-V2 and nnResUNet localized all ostia without failure (>5 mm error), with median errors of 0.70-0.87 mm. Trained on CAT08 and ASOCA alone, SwinUNETR-V2 fails on 34% of right and 53% of left ostia, whereas adding 250 ImageCAS volumes removes all failures. The centerlines were extracted by a deterministic, quality-controlled minimal-path procedure; on ASOCA, they cover a median of 99.5% of the reference length, with a median per-patient mean distance of 0.22 mm between matched reference points and centerlines. Annotations, centerlines, code, and weights are available at https://hal9000-lab.github.io/.

papers.title: SmartBloch-Agent: An Agentic Framework for Automated MRI Sequence Design and Optimization
papers.summary: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) pulse sequences organize radiofrequency excitation, gradient encoding, and signal acquisition, determining magnetization evolution and image formation. Sequence research requires translating imaging objectives into executable protocols meeting physical and acquisition constraints, refined via physical simulation, signal reconstruction, and scientific evaluation. Sequence construction, physical verification, parameter search, and assessment involve many tools and manual decisions, limiting automation from objective to verifiable sequence. We develop SmartBloch-Agent, an integrated framework for automated MRI sequence design and optimization. Given objectives and scientific constraints in natural language, an AI agent interprets goals, plans tasks, orchestrates tools, and makes feedback-informed decisions, drawing on a construction module and optimizers for structural design and parameter search. Our GPU-accelerated SmartBloch engine supplies physical computation for both stages, so the framework configures, per sequence and objective, event validation, Full-Bloch magnetization evolution, signal acquisition, image reconstruction, and scientific evaluation, and closes the loop without external MRI simulators. Results return to the agent to guide sequence revision, parameter optimization, and candidate selection, and the design files carry simulation, reconstruction, and evaluation evidence, forming an output package for a real-scanner workflow. Experiments show the framework automatically designs and optimizes MRI sequences for varied objectives and constraints, refines candidates with physical feedback, and improves several parameter-estimation metrics and downstream quantitative reconstruction. SmartBloch-Agent unifies objectives, design, physical execution, and evaluation into a continuous workflow for end-to-end automation of MRI sequence research.

papers.title: Semantic Extraction Framework for Goal-Oriented V2X Communication Supporting Safe Intersection Passage
papers.summary: This paper proposes a transmitter-side semantic extraction framework for goal-oriented Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) communication supporting safe intersection passage. Instead of transmitting raw sensory data, roadside infrastructure extracts task-relevant semantic information from video and traffic-signal sequences and organizes them into compact semantic packets for low-latency driving-decision assistance. The intersection-passing problem is formulated as a set of traffic tasks under Japanese traffic regulations, and the proposed pipeline generates perception and intent semantics through object detection, object tracking, region-of-interest (ROI)-based semantic extraction, and recommended-action generation. The framework is implemented and evaluated on a self-constructed, CARLA-based single-vehicle dataset collected under clear weather conditions. Experimental results show high recommended-action accuracy within the tested task set, while the mean processing latency remains below the frame interval of the 15~fps input video.

papers.title: Quantifying System-Level Performance Bottlenecks in Hyperspectral Target Detection
papers.summary: Discerning core performance bottlenecks in hyperspectral target detection is highly challenging given the complex interplay between sub-systems of the imaging chain (scene, atmosphere, sensor and processing). Prior sensitivity and limitation studies offer narrow insights applicable to specific system configurations. To address the need for broader generalization, an analysis framework was constructed to quantify limitations from large ensembles of model scenarios. Key components of the framework include the use of canonical scene representations and the log-weighted area under the ROC curve (wAUC), a metric well-suited for rare target detection. By analyzing thousands of scenarios, parametric thresholds were quantified where detection performance degrades, corresponding to "knees" in performance curves. A knee significance score (KSS) is introduced to assess the relative importance of these thresholds. The framework an airborne VNIR sensor implanted in 28,000 scenarios using seven system parameters spanning the scene, atmosphere and sensor. Results suggest that aerosol visibility in the 2-6 km range is the dominant limiter in detection, followed by subpixel target percentages of 15-35%, and background clutter modeled using a t-distribution with 3-5 degrees of freedom.

papers.title: Measurement-Aware Multimodal LLM for No-Reference Low-Dose CT Quality Assessment
papers.summary: No-reference image quality assessment (IQA) of low-dose CT predicts the score that radiologists would assign to a slice without a full-dose reference, as needed to compare dose protocols and denoisers. Trained CT IQA networks agree well with radiologists but output only a score, whereas multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can explain a score but perform poorly on CT when only prompted. We propose a measurement-aware MLLM, built on Qwen3.8-27B, that rates a slice from its image together with six image-domain measurements of noise, sharpness, high-frequency content and streaks, given to the language model as percentiles in text. On the LDCT-IQA 2023 test set, it reaches an Overall score of 2.735, on par with the retrained challenge winner (2.735) and MedSigLIP-FiLM (2.713), and substantially above its base MLLM used as a zero-shot agent. Shuffling the measurements at test time reduces the score by 0.048, mostly through noise, but the same measurements also lead the model to assign higher scores to over-smoothed denoised images.

papers.title: eSharp: Diffusion-based Sharp Monocular Metric Event-to-Depth Estimation
papers.summary: Depth perception is fundamental for autonomous navigation, industrial inspection, and mixed-reality systems. It often operates under strict constraints on power and form factor. In such cases, monocular depth estimation (MDE) is often used. Even as recent advances continue to improve monocular depth quality, conventional frame-based MDE systems remain challenged by fast motion and high-dynamic-range scenes. This work introduces eSharp, an MDE framework that addresses these problems using an event camera. eSharp repurposes pretrained diffusion priors for event-only MDE and produces accurate metric depth with unparalleled sharpness on real data. Real-world event datasets provide only sparse LiDAR depth maps for ground-truth supervision, making dense prediction challenging. We address this limitation through cross-modal distillation, using LiDAR-calibrated dense pseudo-labels generated from a spatially co-registered frame camera to train eSharp. Experiments show that eSharp outperforms prior event-to-depth baselines in both metric-depth accuracy and spatial fidelity, establishing diffusion models as a promising foundation for event-driven 3D perception.

papers.title: Edge-Assisted Crowdsensing for Explainable Cyclist Safety Perception
papers.summary: Cyclist fatality rates remain high despite policy support for active travel, and autonomous vehicles add complexity to mixed traffic. Neither crash statistics nor multi-model detection pipelines scale to continuous monitoring of perceived safety along a route. We present an edge-assisted crowdsensing system: handlebar cameras supply street-level frames, a vision-language model (VLM) turns each frame into structured traffic attributes through a single prompt, and an explainable boosting machine (EBM) combines them with OpenStreetMap road infrastructure and on-bike kinematics to predict a crowdsourced 1-9 safety score. Extraction belongs at the network edge: the fastest self-hosted model needs 2.49 s per frame and scoring takes 0.4 ms on a CPU. On 1,362 annotated frames from two London routes, the EBM regressor reaches 72.2 percent binary accuracy and a mean absolute error of 1.011 under five-fold cross-validation. It is within one accuracy point of black-box ensembles. Its per-feature shape functions give exact attribution: physical lane separation is worth +0.97 rating points, a painted lane +0.70 and a construction site -0.65. Planners can therefore price an infrastructure change in rating points, and the results enter cost-benefit analysis directly. We also report inter-annotator agreement (alpha = 0.4695), an attribute audit, and a sensitivity analysis linking attribute error to accuracy. With re-encoding, a 20 s sampling interval serves 1,000 riders at 54 Mbit/s at a cost of 1.4 accuracy points, making continuous monitoring practical.

papers.title: OraRefer: Segmentation-Guided Multi-Photograph Fusion for Oral Cancer Screening with Guaranteed Patient-Level Sensitivity
papers.summary: Oral cancer and the oral potentially malignant disorders (OPMD) that can precede it are visible on the oral mucosa, which makes smartphone photographs a promising tool for screening. Deep learning models for this task classify individual photographs. However, screening refers patients, not photographs: a patient is usually photographed several times, and the referral decision must miss no more than a set share of patients with disease. We propose OraRefer, a patient-level screening model that reads each photograph with a segmentation-guided foundation model that conditions its class decision on the predicted lesion, combines all photographs of a patient with risk factors, and refers through a threshold with a finite-sample sensitivity guarantee. The model localizes the mouth itself, so inference needs no annotation. On 3000 photographs of 714 patients, patient-level fusion reaches an AUROC of 0.919 and outperforms attention-based multiple-instance learning. At a 90% sensitivity target, OraRefer detects 95% of patients with OPMD or cancer and misses 3 of 61 patients with cancer, at a specificity of 0.610. Because the threshold is calibrated without retraining, each clinic can set its own guaranteed operating point on a local calibration sample.

papers.title: Interpretable Multimodal MRI-Clinical Fusion for Functional Outcome Prediction After Acute Ischemic Stroke
papers.summary: This study evaluates the added prognostic value of day-1 multimodal MRI for predicting three-month functional outcome after acute ischemic stroke (AIS). Sixty-six AIS patients with ADC, DWI, FLAIR, and clinical data were analyzed. Three-dimensional pretrained ResNet embeddings were extracted from each MRI modality, reduced using fold-isolated principal component analysis, and combined with structured clinical variables and ADC-derived lesion biomarkers. Linear support vector machines were evaluated using eight-fold stratified group cross-validation across MRI modality combinations. Clinical-only modeling achieved strong performance (AUC = $0.899 \pm 0.151$), while MRI-only models showed limited discrimination (AUC $\approx$ $0.67$-$0.73$). Among multimodal configurations, FLAIR-clinical fusion achieved the highest mean cross-validated performance (AUC = $0.948 \pm 0.061$), followed by ADC-clinical fusion (AUC = $0.941 \pm 0.094$). Full ADC-DWI-FLAIR fusion did not consistently outperform single-modality clinical fusion. Feature-importance analysis identified age, NIHSS subscores, ADC lesion burden, and learned FLAIR representations as key contributors, while qualitative FLAIR activation maps showed responses over lesion-like regions. These findings suggest that compact day-1 FLAIR and ADC representations provide complementary prognostic information beyond clinical variables and support interpretable, data-efficient outcome prediction in AIS.

papers.title: Simulation of Refraction Through Voxel Volumes
papers.summary: Ray tracing in X-ray science has typically been limited to descriptions where refraction occurs only at interfaces, ignoring the refraction occurring due to the continuous variations in index of refraction in the bulk of a material, as are common in biological samples like bone. We propose a method to simulate X-ray images directly on voxel grids using curved rays. We first validate this method compared to a model with an analytical solution, and then investigate the effects of voxel size, interpolation choice, and illumination to grid alignment on a few simulated test objects. From these investigations, we make several recommendations to guide simulations using these techniques.

papers.title: GenStrain: Multi-Conditional Generative Diffusion Model To Synthesize High-quality Motion and Strain Maps From Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Images
papers.summary: This paper presents GenStrain, a novel method for synthesizing high-quality cardiac motion-based strain maps from routinely collected cine cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) images. Existing approaches typically rely on image registration to estimate motion (a sequence of displacements) from cine CMR images, but cine CMR presents very sparse trackable intramyocardial features, presenting challenges to estimate intramyocardial motion. An advanced imaging technique, Displacement Encoding with Stimulated Echoes (DENSE) CMR, is considered as the gold standard for strain assessment, but it requires additional acquisitions, which are not ideal for efficient clinical workflows. To address this gap, we introduce GenStrain, a novel framework designed to learn the data distribution of highly accurate cardiac motion captured by DENSE. In particular, we develop a diffusion process in motion space, where spatiotemporal continuity is carefully considered. To fully leverage both cine CMR images and their associated motion patterns, we introduce a multi-conditional conditioning strategy that integrates anatomical features and motion representations learned by a spatiotemporal registration model to guide the generation process. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed model, GenStrain, outperforms existing strain analysis methods based on displacement estimates from both traditional registration approaches and state-of-the-art (SOTA) deep learning models. Our model represents a promising step toward more accurate cardiac function assessment and holds great potential for clinical translation. Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/Rishov-MIA/GenStrain.

papers.title: RapidMitDet: Boosting Computational Efficiency for Mitosis Detection via Magnification Alignment
papers.summary: Automated mitosis detection is a critical research focus, enabling pathologists to rapidly assess mitotic indices for tumor malignancy evaluation. However, most of the existing detection approaches suffer from significant computational inefficiency due to the giga-pixel image resolution of Whole-Slide Images (WSIs), which greatly hinders their clinical applicability. In this study, we propose RapidMitDet, a computational efficient mitosis detection approach. Our method employs a coarse-to-fine framework, first identifying mitotic candidates at lower magnification and then confirming them at higher magnification. In the coarse-detection stage, we introduce magnification-aligned knowledge distillation to reduce the information gap between magnification levels while minimizing the performance degradation in the lower magnification detection model. In the subsequent fine-classification stage, we propose adaptive triplet learning (ATL) to optimize infomative sample selection, thereby enhancing discrimination between mitotic and non-mitotic instances. Experimental results show that RapidMitDet achieves the optimal accuracy-efficiency balance at 20x magnification, improving computational speed by up to 5.62 times over the latest state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods. Due to its lightweight model design, RapidMitDet can also deliver efficient detection at higher magnification (40x) while achieving even higher detection performance. In WSI-level evaluations, our method shows strong agreement with pathologists' diagnoses (ICCs: 0.879 (40x), 0.822 (20x)) while maintaining superior efficiency, highlighting its potential for clinical application. Code is available at https://github.com/logincat/RapidMitDet

papers.title: Volumetric Latent Diffusion for Brain Tumour Segmentation with Missing Modalities
papers.summary: Brain tumour segmentation from magnetic resonance imaging normally assumes that all four imaging sequences are available, but in clinical practice one or more are frequently missing. Existing methods for incomplete inputs learn modality-invariant representations or distil from a full-modality teacher, and return a single deterministic mask. Gen- erative formulations instead model a distribution over plausible masks, but the cost of sampling at full resolution has largely confined them to two dimensions. This paper proposes a three-dimensional conditional latent diffusion framework for whole-tumour segmentation from incom- plete multi-sequence MRI. Images and annotations are first compressed by two volumetric autoencoders, which makes diffusion over whole vol- umes affordable, and sequences are dropped at random during training so that a single model handles every combination of missing sequences. Because the model samples rather than predicts, repeated draws also yield a voxel-wise map of disagreement at no extra training cost. Evalu- ations on 2,601 studies from BraTS 2023 and 2024 show that the method reaches 0.955 Dice with all four sequences and 0.904 with FLAIR alone, and that it is the most accurate of the four methods compared in eight of the fifteen configurations. The disagreement between draws widens as sequences are withheld, giving a signal that accompanies the prediction rather than replacing it

papers.title: Subliminal Learning in Vision-Language Models
papers.summary: Subliminal learning is a phenomenon in large language models (LLMs) where a teacher passes a hidden preference to a student through training data unrelated to that preference. We study whether subliminal learning also occurs in vision-language models (VLMs). We finetune a teacher VLM to prefer a specific animal or facial attribute and use a control teacher from the same base model. Both teachers generate numbers for an unrelated visual task involving geometric shapes. Two students initialized from the same base VLM are finetuned on the same images, using numbers generated by either the biased or control teacher. Across VLMs ranging from 2B to 7B parameters, we find that both animal and facial preferences can transfer through this unrelated task. Students trained on biased-teacher outputs select the target more often than control students, with a difference of up to $\sim$10 percentage points in the animal preference task. Transfer can become stronger with more training data and varies with the target preference, model, and how the numbers are generated. Beyond preferences, we show that the biased student's explanations use more of the same words and phrases as the biased teacher's explanations than those of the control student, even when all three models select the same image. These results matter for training VLMs and show that training on unrelated data may change both a VLM's image preferences and how it explains its choices, and that transfer can become stronger with more training samples.

papers.title: CNVAE: Anatomically Correct Segmentation via Conditional Generative Modeling
papers.summary: Supervised deep learning segmentation models, although unparalleled in performance, are not immune to anatomical mistakes. We develop a segmentation-by-generation paradigm extending the Nouveau VAE (NVAE) generative framework for anatomically correct cardiac segmentation. In particular, we propose a novel conditional NVAE model (CNVAE) for conditional shape generation, and explore its capabilities for image segmentation in two scenarios: (1) direct image-to-mask CNVAE for one-step segmentation; (2) mask-to-mask CNVAE for refinement of segmentation masks produced by third-party segmentation models. Both models are lightweight and return consistently anatomically valid segmentation masks (> 98% success rate, an improvement of 15% above state-of-the-art segmentation models) on the cardiac segmentation/editing tasks of interest, without loss of accuracy in segmented contours.

papers.title: SideAge-RiskNet: Predicted Mammographic-Age Features for Future Breast Cancer Risk and Laterality Prediction
papers.summary: Whether breast-specific mammographic aging provides information beyond chronological age for future cancer prediction remains unclear. We propose SideAge-RiskNet, a framework integrating predicted mammographic-age features with breast-specific representations for multi-year breast cancer risk and conditional laterality prediction. A side-aware DenseNet121 trained on never-cancer reference examinations estimates left and right breast ages. Age-adjusted residuals and bilateral age descriptors are subsequently fused with corresponding image representations, while clinical variables contribute through an image--clinical risk branch. The framework jointly predicts cumulative cancer risk over 1--5 years and the subsequently affected breast among unilateral cancer cases. Across 4,480 EMBED and 248 external examinations, pre-cancer scans demonstrated pronounced bilateral age asymmetry. SideAge-RiskNet established state-of-the-art performance in 1--5-year risk assessment over Mirai and AsymMirai with mean risk AUROCs of 81.73% on EMBED and 72.83% on CSMC. Furthermore, it enabled conditional cancer laterality prediction, achieving AUROCs of 73.26% and 82.53%, respectively. This demonstrates the critical utility of bilateral aging phenotypes in localized breast cancer risk surveillance.

papers.title: Destructive augmentations for prostate lesion segmentation on heterogeneous biparametric MRI data
papers.summary: Training prostate lesion segmentation models on biparametric MRI (bpMRI) is limited by small datasets with heterogeneous imaging acquisition protocols and annotations. In this work, we train a segmentation model on a combined cohort of 1,579 lesion-containing training cases from five datasets, representing, to our knowledge, the largest collection of prostate lesion annotations used for this task. Additionally, we investigate two complementary improvements to the widely used nnU-Net framework. First, we introduce a random wavelet augmentation and show that random sym4 (Symlet) wavelets outperform random convolution augmentation in terms of average Dice score, with only a modest reduction in F1 score due to lower precision. Second, we evaluate instance-level losses and show that Connected-Component-based Dice (CC-Dice)-CE loss complements BackSplit, yielding better performance than BackSplit alone. Together, these improvements achieve the best overall performance, reaching a Dice score of 0.614 on the public Prostate158 test set and establishing a new state-of-the-art on this benchmark. We publicly release our training code and model weights.

papers.title: Finite Element Elastographic Analysis of Kidney MRI for Computational Assessment of Chronic Kidney Disease
papers.summary: Background and Objective: Bridging kidney MRI with patient-specific computational biomechanics may enable accurate, noninvasive assessment of chronic kidney disease. To develop a finite element method (FEM)-based computational elastography framework for estimating renal biomechanical properties from conventional kidney MRI and to evaluate its ability to differentiate chronic kidney disease (CKD) from healthy controls. Methods: Kidney segmentation masks from healthy control and CKD subjects were converted into triangulated surface meshes, and watertight surfaces were tetrahedralized to create volumetric FEM meshes. Kidney tissue was modeled as a nearly incompressible Kelvin-Voigt viscoelastic material. Harmonic wave propagation simulations were performed using FEM, followed by Helmholtz-based elastographic inversion to estimate complex shear modulus distributions. Derived biomechanical parameters were used for CKD classification using machine learning models. Results: FEM-derived stiffness estimates showed consistency with stiffness ranges previously reported in human renal MRE studies and also showed measurable differences between healthy and CKD groups. Machine learning models trained on FEM-derived features achieved classification performance up to 86.26% cross-validation accuracy with an AUC of 0.92. Conclusion: FEM-derived elastographic parameters showed potential for distinguishing CKD from healthy tissue and may provide an alternative for renal biomechanical assessment without dedicated MRE acquisition.

papers.title: Arctic-SAR: A Cross-Sensor RADARSAT Constellation Mission and Sentinel-1 Dataset and Fusion Benchmark for Multi-Task Sea Ice Mapping
papers.summary: Current sea ice mapping benchmarks are mostly built around single-sensor SAR products, limiting the evaluation of cross-sensor variability and the effectiveness of combining observations from different SAR platforms. Models trained on such datasets may also be sensitive to sensor-specific artifacts, radiometric characteristics, and acquisition conditions, which can reduce robustness and limit generalization. To address these limitations, this study introduces Arctic-SAR, a cross-sensor SAR dataset for Arctic sea ice mapping, constructed by matching RADARSAT Constellation Mission (RCM) dual-polarization imagery with Sentinel-1 scenes from the AI4Arctic Sea Ice Dataset. The dataset consists of 221 co-registered scenes and supports multi-task prediction of sea ice concentration (SIC), stage of development (SOD), and floe size (FLOE). In addition to the dataset, we establish a benchmark for cross-sensor SAR sea ice mapping by quantifying the contribution of RCM imagery and evaluating single-sensor baselines alongside representative input-, feature-, and decision-level fusion strategies within a consistent multi-task U-Net framework. Across three independent runs, the test results show that the effectiveness of cross-sensor fusion is strongly dependent on the fusion strategy and prediction task. Decision-level fusion achieves the highest mean combined score of $77.28\pm0.29\%$, essentially matching the Sentinel-1-only baseline at $77.26\pm0.13\%$, while achieving the highest SIC \(R^2\) score. These findings show that Sentinel-1 and RCM provide task- and class-dependent information, but that simple joint cross-sensor fusion does not consistently improve generalization over a strong single-sensor baseline. Arctic-SAR therefore provides a benchmark for cross-sensor SAR fusion research in automated Arctic sea ice mapping.

papers.title: Task-Aware Bitrate Thresholds for Codec-Robust Ultrasound Segmentation
papers.summary: Remote robot surgery and tele-ultrasound increasingly rely on real-time streaming under strict bandwidth constraints, making lossy compression unavoidable. Since the receiving end of these clinical pipelines is increasingly a machine rather than a human observer, codec selection must be guided by downstream task accuracy rather than perceptual fidelity. We evaluate three widely deployed codecs, H.264/AVC, HEVC, and AV1, on prostate ultrasound segmentation, reporting task-aware compression performance with region overlap (Dice) and boundary accuracy (HD95) as the quality metrics. To compare codecs fairly, we match their operating points at a common perceptual-quality (SSIM) level. We establish, per codec, the lowest bitrate that preserves acceptable segmentation accuracy, reporting the 5th-percentile Dice alongside the mean to expose worst-case degradation. All three codecs preserve segmentation quality (mean Dice $\geq$ 0.84) down to approximately 0.07-0.20 bits per voxel (bpv). Below this point, AV1's accuracy declines gradually, while H.264's drops sharply. As a result, H.264 needs 82% more bitrate than AV1 to reach the same region-overlap accuracy (Dice), and 104.7% more to reach the same boundary accuracy (HD95).
papers.comment: It is already accepted at IEEE Visual Communications and Image Processing Conference

papers.title: A Frame-Level View and Image-Quality Annotation Tool for Fetal Echocardiography: Comparison with Spreadsheet Annotation
papers.summary: Objective: To develop the Cardiologist Annotation Tool (CAT) for frame-level cardiac view and image-quality annotation in fetal echocardiography and compare it with spreadsheet-based annotation. Methods: CAT provides cine playback, frame navigation, and keyboard-based labeling without manual frame-range entry. Experts annotated 25 studies using both methods, and spreadsheet annotations were audited for predefined data-entry errors. In a randomized crossover study, six medical students annotated two normal studies, one with each method, against an expert reference. Results: Among 1,746 spreadsheet-annotated files, 6.2% contained major or critical data-entry errors, more frequently in congenital heart disease than normal studies (10.9% vs 3.4%). CAT yielded more annotated view segments per clip (3.6 vs 1.5). Rates of labeled and correctly labeled frames per minute were 1.77 and 1.68 times those with spreadsheets, respectively (both P = 0.031), with gains in all six students. No detectable difference in view-label accuracy was observed. Conclusion: CAT eliminates manual frame-range entry and enables finer-grained, structured annotation of fetal echocardiography, providing a practical approach to preparing datasets for AI research.

papers.title: From Vision to Context: A Review of Prompt-Driven Target Volume Segmentation in Radiotherapy
papers.summary: Accurate target volume (TV) segmentation is essential for radiotherapy (RT) planning but remains time-consuming. Moreover, the final contour depends on the expertise of the radiation oncologist. Although deep learning has improved medical image segmentation, image-only models cannot encode the clinical reasoning that governs TV delineation, particularly for the clinical target volume (CTV), where boundaries are defined by clinical knowledge rather than imaging features alone. Prompt-driven segmentation has recently emerged as a strategy to address this limitation. This work aims to review these approaches for RT TV segmentation with four objectives: (1) compare the different prompting techniques used; (2) compare their performance against image-only baselines; (3) assess how they are evaluated against standard metrics, including the Dice similarity coefficient (DSC), 95th Hausdorff distance, sensitivity, precision, and clinical assessment; and (4) identify the gaps needed for clinical translation. We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, and arXiv for studies incorporating geometric, clinical text, or interactive prompts into deep learning models for RT TV delineation. Thirteen studies met the inclusion criteria, spanning head and neck, breast, prostate, lung, cervix, and rectal cancers. Seven studies used clinical text prompting, four used geometric prompting, and two used interactive prompting; three combined modalities. Reported DSC ranged from 0.67 to 0.93, compared to 0.65 to 0.91 for image-only baselines. None reported sensitivity or precision. Clinical text prompting appears well suited to CTV delineation. Evidence remains limited, and standardized prompt engineering and clinical validation are needed before these approaches can be translated into routine RT practice.
